live.name: literal_listener
live.hypothesis: Listeners pick uniformly among the objects the word is literally true of.

live.name: rsa_l1
live.hypothesis: Listeners invert a softmax-rational speaker who simulates a literal listener (depth 1), with a uniform prior over objects.

live.name: rsa_l2
live.hypothesis: Listeners reason one level deeper (depth 2), inverting a speaker who simulates the depth-1 pragmatic listener.

live.name: rsa_l1_salience
live.hypothesis: Depth-1 RSA whose listener has a salience prior over objects (feature count, familiarization base rate) that the simulated literal listener lacks.

live.name: rsa_l1_shared_prior
live.hypothesis: Depth-1 RSA with the salience prior as common knowledge, used by the simulated literal listener as well as the pragmatic listener.

events.name: feature_parsimony_heuristic
events.hypothesis: Listeners interpret referring expressions using a non-Bayesian feature-parsimony heuristic rather than recursive Theory of Mind. When hearing a feature word, listeners select among the objects of which the word is literally true by penalizing objects that possess superfluous unmentioned features, exponentially preferring the most minimal referent. On trials without an informative word, listeners choose uniformly among available objects.

events.name: singleton_isolation_listener
events.hypothesis: Listeners exhibit an isolation preference, placing high prior expectation on contextually unique singletons over objects with identical duplicates in the display. On displays containing two identical objects and one singleton where a shared feature is heard, this predicts listeners will predominantly choose the singleton, whereas RSA depth-2 predicts listeners will choose the duplicate objects because a speaker intending the singleton would have used its unique feature.

events.name: discriminative_alternative_speaker
events.hypothesis: Speakers experience a communicative penalty when choosing an ambiguous word if a uniquely distinguishing word for their intended referent was available in the visual context. Pragmatic listeners invert this speaker, recognizing that a speaker who uses an ambiguous word either had no distinguishing alternative or faced production costs, driving pragmatic reference resolution.

events.name: rsa_l2_shared_prior
events.hypothesis: Listeners reason at depth 2 (inverting a speaker who simulates a pragmatic listener) while treating object salience—driven by feature count and familiarization base rates—as common knowledge across all levels of recursion. By sharing the salience prior among the literal listener, both simulated speakers, and the pragmatic listener (and defaulting to this prior on prior trials), the model accounts for contextual object preferences and prior elicitation while preserving depth-2 pragmatic implicature. Compared to rsa_l2, recursion depth remains at L2, two parameters (w_features and w_familiar) are added to form the shared salience prior via softmax, the object prior at every level (L0, S1, S2, and L2) changes from uniform to this salience prior, and choices on prior trials evaluate to this prior rather than uniform guessing.

events.name: rsa_l2_salience
events.hypothesis: We refine rsa_l2 by incorporating an asymmetric object salience prior (taking the salience prior component from rsa_l1_salience) at the depth-2 pragmatic listener level: listeners combine depth-2 recursive pragmatic reasoning with a subjective salience prior over referents based on feature counts and familiarization base rates, while modeling simulated lower-level agents as reasoning with uniform object priors. This allows listeners to capture contextual exposure and perceptual biases—and predict non-uniform choices on uninformative prior trials—without assuming that lower-level literal and pragmatic reasoning is biased by referent salience. Compared to rsa_l2, recursion depth remains at L2, two parameters (w_features and w_familiar) are added to construct the salience prior, the prior enters the top-level speaker simulation S2 in L2 as a prior over referents (while L0 and S1 retain uniform object priors), and choices on prior trials evaluate to this salience prior rather than uniform guessing.

events.hypothesis: We refine rsa_l1_shared_prior by incorporating an isolation preference for contextually unique singletons (taking the singleton isolation component from singleton_isolation_listener) into the shared object prior: listeners and the speakers they model treat unique singletons lacking identical duplicates in the visual display as salient referents alongside familiar and feature-sparse objects.
